t: The Opera Comique no longer exists, but this is the area where it stood, between Wych Street, Holywell Street and the Strand. The theatre opened in 1870 and was demolished in 1902 to make way for Aldwych and Kingsway. It was designed by the architect Francis Fowler, who later had to resign from the Metropolitan Board of Works after being found guilty of corruption. Its owner, Sefton Henry Parry, was a versatile Victorian theatre manager, an actor, playwright and scenery painter, and a builder of theatres.
